Let’s look ahead with Chapter 10: Looking Forward—The Unfinished Work of Justice.
The story of women, race, and class in America? It’s anything but simple. It’s full of struggle and resilience, progress and setbacks, dreams that have been put on hold—and others that have finally come true. The victories we’ve seen at the ballot box, in the workplace, and through the courts? Those are real, no question about it. But so are the challenges that still stand in our way.
Think about it—every time a new law is passed, new barriers seem to show up. And for every strong coalition that’s built, there are old divisions that still need healing. Justice isn’t a one-and-done deal—it’s ongoing. It asks for our constant attention, a healthy dose of humility, and a willingness to really learn from what’s happened before.
Imagine a group of friends, gathered together after a long day spent organizing for change. They’re tired for sure, but there’s hope in the air. They know the road ahead won’t be easy. But here’s the thing—they know they’re not walking it alone. They draw strength from each other, from the stories of those who’ve come before, and from that deep belief that a better world really is possible.
There’s a lesson here that’s worth remembering. Justice isn’t something handed out like a gift—it’s something you have to fight for, side by side. The fight for women’s rights, for racial justice, for economic equality? It’s all one struggle, not separate battles. It’s a story that belongs to all of us, and here’s the best part—it’s still being written.
